tables.title: The week's headline moves beside their numerators — with and without the Monday pair
tables.note: Mon 09-07 was US Labor Day: US DAU 24,085 that day against 12,711 on Mon 09-14. The last column drops that one pair so the holiday cannot carry a comparison.
tables.source: series.json headline series (settled, no FILLED_ZERO) via tools/lib.js daily()/byBreakdown(); new/returning from reports/2026-09-19/data/brainrot.json explore.specs (DailyActiveUsers × IsNewUser). Mean of paired days, POST day d vs PRE day d−7.

tables.title: Week-on-week change by day, 05 → 17 Sep: which series moved before the 11 Sep publish
tables.note: Each cell is that day against the same weekday a week earlier. Russia, new-user DAU and Home impressions are already up by 09-08 → 09-10, before v612 (09-11 15:51 UTC). GamePass revenue is up w/w through 09-11 and down every day from 09-12. D1 and revenue lag, so their newest cells are blank.
tables.source: series.json via tools/lib.js (DailyActiveUsers, DailyActiveUsers×Country, UniqueUsersWithImpressions×AcquisitionSource, ForwardD1Retention, AverageSessionLengthMinutes, DailyRevenue×RevenueSource, PayingUsers, ClientCrashRate15m); new-user DAU from Explore. Δ = day / (day−7) − 1.

tables.title: Event, creative and engine calendar in each window
rows: RCC 738 on 09-08 22:36 and 09-09 16:47, between the windows
tables.note: Both windows carry one admin-abuse Saturday, one NEW UPDATE listing and a Saturday icon rotation, so those items are present on both sides of every comparison.
tables.source: reports/2026-09-19/data/brainrot.json annotations + placeVersions (annotations.md, place-versions.csv).

tables.title: Place-icon changes by Saturday since 25 Jul
tables.note: Icons changed on 8 of 8 Saturdays and on 0 non-Saturdays in this span, so an icon change never occurs without the admin-abuse Saturday beside it and cannot be event-studied on its own.
tables.source: data/games/9963622286/annotations.md, ANNOTATION_TYPE_PLACE_ICON, de-duplicated on (time, type, metadata).

tables.title: Where the added DAU came from, by country (12 largest movers)
tables.note: Russia alone is 39% of the week's added DAU; the US is the largest faller. Country rows sum to within ~0.5% of the headline (Explore reconciliation), so shares are approximate.
tables.source: DailyActiveUsers × Country (ONE_DAY, whole population) from series.json; 5 paired days each side.

tables.title: Russia's share of DAU by day — Brainrot against the other four games
tables.note: Brainrot's Russian share steps from 6–7% to 15.5% on Tue 09-08 and reaches 24.6% on 09-17. No other game in the portfolio moves this way.
tables.source: DailyActiveUsers × Country (RU) ÷ headline DailyActiveUsers, each game's series.json.

tables.title: The added DAU by acquisition source and by new vs returning
tables.note: HomeRecommendation carries 78% of the added DAU and new users 65%. Search DAU fell 4.9%. Segment rows come from different breakdowns and reconcile to the headline within ~3% (new + returning shares sum to 103%). Home impressions grew faster (+65.5%) than Home DAU (+46.6%), so conversion per Home impression fell while the volume rose.
tables.source: DailyActiveUsers × AcquisitionSource and UniqueUsersWithImpressions × AcquisitionSource (series.json); IsNewUser from Explore; source rows under 50 DAU omitted.

tables.title: Thumbnail changes against the base rate of ordinary days
columns: Series (w/w change on the day after a change)
tables.note: Change dates: 07-16, 07-21, 08-03, 08-10, 08-12, 08-20, 08-25, 09-01, 09-06, 09-10, 09-13. |z| under 2 means the day after a thumbnail change is not distinguishable from any other day.
tables.source: ANNOTATION_TYPE_PLACE_THUMBNAIL dates from annotations.md; series from series.json; window 07-22 → 09-17; w/w = day ÷ same weekday −7d − 1; z = (mean after change − ordinary mean) ÷ (ordinary SD ÷ √n).

tables.title: Mean concurrents per day, matched weekday (half-hour series, all 48 slots)
tables.note: Saturday, the admin-abuse day, is excluded from the trend line. The daily-peak series the chart shows moved +33.4% on the same pairs.
tables.source: PeakConcurrentPlayers HALF_HOUR (reports/2026-09-19/data/ccu-9963622286.json, pulled 2026-09-19 09:01 UTC), mean of the 48 half-hour peaks per UTC day.

tables.title: Today (Sat 09-19, partial) against the last two Saturdays, same UTC half-hours
tables.note: Only the slots that had finished when the series was pulled (09:01 UTC) are compared; the 09:00 bucket was partial and the 09:30 bucket repeated it (carry-forward), so both are dropped. All slots are before the 15:00 admin-abuse hour.
tables.source: PeakConcurrentPlayers HALF_HOUR, ccu-9963622286.json; mean of the peaks in each pair of half-hour slots.

tables.title: Concurrents in the two hours after each publish, against the same clock hours on ordinary days
tables.note: Ordinary days = 08-23 → 09-18 excluding Saturdays and the three publish days. A z near 0 means the publish day's afternoon followed the normal diurnal curve.
tables.source: PeakConcurrentPlayers HALF_HOUR (ccu-9963622286.json); ratio of mean half-hour peak after ÷ before, per day.

tables.title: The Saturday admin-abuse hour (15:00–16:00 UTC), four Saturdays
tables.note: The event multiplies concurrents for one hour and the level falls back by 16:30. Its multiple has shrunk as the base rose.
tables.source: PeakConcurrentPlayers HALF_HOUR (ccu-9963622286.json); ADMIN ABUSE START/END from annotations.md.

tables.title: D1 by acquisition source — effect size and confidence kept separate
tables.note: Relative change is the effect size; z divides the 5-pair mean change by that source's own week-on-week SD (08-15 → 09-09) ÷ √5. Friends and Search are the controls: they do not arrive through the listing.
tables.source: ForwardD1Retention × AcquisitionSource (series.json, ONE_DAY); DAU × AcquisitionSource for volume.

tables.title: D1 by platform class, each against its own earlier weeks
tables.note: Compare each row with itself across the columns, not with the other rows. TV and VR (under 40 DAU) are not read.
tables.source: ForwardD1Retention × Platform and DailyActiveUsers × Platform (series.json); Mobile = DAU-weighted mean of Phone and Tablet per day.

tables.title: Home ranking signals by week, beside Home impressions (Sat→Wed means)
tables.note: Read across each row. Play-through, bounce, D1 playtime and qualified sessions improve in the 09-05→09-09 week, before Home impressions rise in the 09-12→09-16 week. D8–28 play days rose in 09-05→09-09 and returned to its 08-22→09-02 level. The spend signals fall in the last week.
tables.source: RFY* metrics and UniqueUsersWithImpressions × AcquisitionSource (series.json, ONE_DAY); mean of the five Sat→Wed days in each week.

tables.title: Session length and playtime: how much is who showed up, how much is within each group
tables.note: Mix alone = before-week segment values at after-week shares; within-segment alone = after-week segment values at before-week shares. Both groups' sessions lengthened, and the within-segment term is larger than the mix term.
tables.source: Explore AverageSessionLengthMinutes and AveragePlayTimeMinutesPerDAU × IsNewUser; DAU × IsNewUser for the shares (brainrot.json explore.specs).

tables.title: Revenue by source, in Robux and per 1,000 DAU
tables.note: DevProduct Robux held level while DAU rose 37%; GamePass Robux halved. Per player both fell, GamePass by more.
tables.source: DailyRevenue × RevenueSource (series.json, ONE_DAY) ÷ DailyActiveUsers. The ItemMonetizationRevenue hourly roll-up in the Monetization split table double-counts some days (09-07, 09-09, 09-10 read exactly 2× the daily GamePass figure), so this table uses DailyRevenue.

tables.title: GamePass and DevProduct Robux by day, each against the same weekday a week earlier
tables.note: GamePass Robux is above its prior-week weekday on 09-09, 09-10 and 09-11 (+28% to +58%; 09-08 was −33%) and below it on all six days from 09-12 to 09-17 (−44% to −64%). DevProduct is above its prior-week weekday on 3 of those 6 days.
tables.source: DailyRevenue × RevenueSource and DailyActiveUsers (series.json).

tables.title: GamePass per 1,000 DAU by week since June
tables.note: The last row (09-14 → 09-17, 4 days) is the lowest GamePass-per-player week since June; DevProduct per player is also at its low.
tables.source: DailyRevenue × RevenueSource ÷ DailyActiveUsers (series.json), 7-day blocks from 06-01.

tables.title: Payers and revenue by day pair — the count behind PayingUsersCVR
tables.note: Without the Labor Day pair, the number of paying users is flat (+0.3%) while DAU is +37.7%. The summary-row CVR is payers ÷ DAU; the metric PayingUsersCVR is a mean of daily ratios and differs slightly.
tables.source: PayingUsers, PayingUsersCVR, DailyRevenue, DailyActiveUsers (series.json).

tables.title: Paying-user CVR by day pair on all five games — is it us or everyone?
tables.note: PayingUsersCVR fell on all five games this week and stepped down from Mon 09-07 to Tue 09-08 on all five (the before-window Saturday→Monday was the US Labor Day weekend). Brainrot's fall is the second-largest, and it is one of two games whose DAU grew.
tables.source: PayingUsersCVR and DailyActiveUsers from each game's reports/2026-09-19/data/<slug>.json (run + cur).

tables.title: Audience and money deltas on all five games, same pairs
tables.note: On the other four games GamePass and DevProduct moved within 16 points of each other; on Brainrot GamePass is 54 points below DevProduct. Waterslide, the other game whose DAU and new users rose, added paying users.
tables.source: Each game's reports/2026-09-19/data/<slug>.json: metrics[].cur (DailyActiveUsers, PayingUsers, PayingUsersCVR), splits.revenueBySource, explore DailyActiveUsers × IsNewUser. Same five Sat→Wed pairs.

tables.title: Matched size and weekday: Mon–Wed 14–16 Sep against Mon–Wed 24–26 Aug
tables.note: At near-identical DAU (123–127K then, 114–127K now) the game had 846 payers a day then and 647 now (−23.5%). The audience composition differs: Russia's share tripled and the new-user share rose.

tables.title: Dilution arithmetic for PayingUsersCVR (4 day pairs, Labor Day pair excluded)
rows: After, if every added player paid nothing and the rest paid as before
tables.note: The actual after-week rate matches the 'added players paid nothing' case to within 0.003pp. The arithmetic does not identify which players pay.
tables.source: PayingUsers, DailyActiveUsers, DailyActiveUsers × Country (series.json); pairs Sat, Sun, Tue, Wed.

tables.title: Funnel steps read two ways: first read (as charted) and all days re-read on 09-19
columns: Cohort age at first read (before / after)
tables.note: The charted rates are the first settled read of each cohort. The before-week cohorts were first read younger (1.5–3.5 days) than the after-week cohorts (2.7–6.4 days), so on the first read the after-week has had longer to mature. On the 09-19 re-read the before-week cohorts are 10–14 days old and the after-week 3–7 days, which tilts the other way. The two Δ columns bracket the maturity-matched change.
tables.source: FunnelCohortCompletionRate × FunnelStep, one FunnelName filter (series.json, capturedAt per point); 09-19 re-served values from data/games/9963622286/data-quality.md revision rows (only divergences >1% are logged; unlogged days use the kept value).

tables.title: Step-to-step conversion on the rebirth ladder and the last BaseUpgrade steps (first read)
tables.note: Each cell is the later step's cohort completion ÷ the earlier step's, so it reads as 'of those who reached step A, the share who reached step B'. FirstMorph → Rebirth1 is the transition that fell (−1.0pp); Rebirth1 → Rebirth2 and Rebirth2 → Rebirth3 rose.
tables.source: reports/2026-09-19/data/brainrot.json funnels (FunnelCohortCompletionRate, first read, 5 paired days).

tables.title: The publish day and the Saturday after it, first read against the 09-19 re-read
tables.note: The 09-11 spike and the 09-12 dip in the charted series both largely disappear on re-read (Rebirth1 09-12: 42.6% → 50.5%; BaseUpgrade20 09-11: 57.0% → 45.9%). FirstMorph's 97.9% on 09-12 is the one cohort below 99.3% in the run.
tables.source: FunnelCohortCompletionRate (series.json first reads) and data-quality.md 09-19 revision rows.

tables.title: Client-performance deltas with the instrument-fault day removed
columns: Change into the fault day: Brainrot · Waterslide · Monkey · Verity · Seal
tables.note: On 09-08 client FPS and memory collapsed by ~75–90% on four of the five games at once (the F28 telemetry fault; Waterslide's multi-place headline did not), and on 09-15 client CPU time fell 32–68% on all five. Same-day falls of this size on unrelated universes are logged as an instrument fault (COVERAGE.md F28), so those pairs are dropped here. Memory % goes from +14% as charted to a fall once 09-08 is removed.
tables.source: Each game's reports/2026-09-19/data/<slug>.json metrics[].run; COVERAGE.md F28 for 09-08.

tables.title: Client crash rate by platform class, each against its own earlier weeks
tables.note: The fall is on mobile only. Same metric on the other games this week: Brainrot −38% · Waterslide +12% · Banana Monkey +29% · Verity +13% · Seal −2%.
tables.source: ClientCrashRate15m × Platform (Place-filtered) and DailyActiveUsers × Platform (series.json); Mobile = DAU-weighted Phone + Tablet.

tables.title: Client crash rate by day, 01 → 18 Sep
tables.note: The headline rate steps down twice: ~2.5% → ~2.1% on 09-08, then → ~1.4–1.6% from 09-12. Phone and Tablet carry both steps; Computer rises 09-08 → 09-10 and again 09-14 → 09-16. OOM exits are a floor by design (telemetry undercounts); read their direction only.
tables.source: ClientCrashRate15m (headline and × Platform), ClientCrashCount, OomUnexpectedExits (Place-filtered, series.json); DAU not served for 09-18.

tables.title: Errors and warnings by log source, per DAU
tables.note: 09-08 has no ErrorCount point, so the Tuesday pair is missing. Server events on the last three Saturdays: 08-29: 411,964 · 09-05: 1,676,948 · 09-12: 359,170 — the 09-05 Saturday is a one-day server spike (1.68M against ~0.2M on neighbouring days).
tables.source: ErrorCount × LogSource (series.json, Place-filtered, ONE_DAY) ÷ DailyActiveUsers. Unit of ErrorCount is not documented by Roblox; per-DAU is a ratio of events to users.

tables.title: Reviews by period: volume, downvote rate, Cyrillic-script share, device
tables.note: The downvote rate of this game's reviews has sat near 50% for its whole life, so a single build's rate on 4 reviews carries no signal. Cyrillic-script reviews are counted as a check against Russia's DAU share, which tripled from 09-08.

tables.title: Net feedback votes (up − down) per 1,000 DAU
tables.note: The corpus holds this series only as up minus down since 08-06 (the VoteType split stops then), so it cannot give a downvote rate; per player it barely moved.

tables.title: DAU by country and by Russian locale, daily 01 → 17 Sep
tables.note: Russia and the ru_ru locale step up on Tue 09-08 (RU 5,844 → 11,992 in one day); Kazakhstan, Ukraine and Belarus rise more gradually from 09-10; the US holds at 11–14K on weekdays.
tables.source: DailyActiveUsers × Country and × Locale (series.json); new-user DAU from Explore.

tables.title: Brainrot against the other four games, day by day from 08 Sep
tables.note: 1.00 = this game moved exactly like the rest of the portfolio that day; below 1 = worse, above 1 = better (for crash rate, above 1 = more crashes). Each game is first divided by its own 01–07 Sep mean, so shared calendar or platform effects — the 08 Sep payer step, the Labor Day weekend — cancel. Rates are the reliable rows; for DAU and impressions the peers mix growing and decaying games, so read those rows as 'moved differently from the portfolio', not as a counterfactual.
tables.source: `run` series in reports/2026-09-19/data/<slug>.json (settled ONE_DAY headline). Index = (this game ÷ its own 01–07 Sep mean) ÷ median over the other four games of the same ratio. tools/r0919/peer-index.js
